questions.text: हड़प्पा संस्कृति के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कथन सही है?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following is the correct statement regarding Harappan Culture?

options.A: अधिकांश हड़प्पा स्थल अर्ध-शुष्क क्षेत्रों में स्थित थे।
options.B: हड़प्पा स्थलों में संभवतः कृषि के लिए सिंचाई की आवश्यकता नहीं पड़ती थी।
options.C: हड़प्पा पुरास्थलों में नहरों के अवशेष नहीं मिले हैं।
options.D: हड़प्पा पुरास्थलों में लोहे के फाल हलों का प्रयोग किया जाता था।

options_english.A: Most of the Harappan sites were located in semi-arid lands.
options_english.B: Irrigation was probably not required for agriculture at the Harappan sites.
options_english.C: No trace of canals have been found at the Harappan sites.
options_english.D: The Iron tipped Ploughshare was used at the Harappan sites.

questions.solution: Option A is correct because archaeological evidence shows that Harappan settlements were primarily located in semi-arid regions where irrigation was essential. Option B is incorrect as irrigation was necessary for farming in these areas. Option C is wrong because canals have been found, such as at Shortughai. Option D is incorrect as the Harappans used terracotta models of ploughs and stone/copper tools, not iron, as iron technology came later.
questions.chapter: Bricks, Beads and Bones: The Harappan Civilisation

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सेना के पूर्व-ब्रिगेडियर और भारतीय पुरातात्विक सर्वेक्षण के डायरेक्टर जनरल थे?
questions.text_english: Who among the following was an ex-army official and worked as Director General of Archaeological Survey of India (ASI)?
questions.solution: R.E.M. Wheeler was an ex-army official who brought the rigid, scientific discipline of military expertise to archaeology. He served as the Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India. John Marshall was a professional archaeologist, Cunningham was the first DG, and Bannerjee discovered Mohenjodaro, but none fit the 'ex-army official' description as accurately as Wheeler.
questions.chapter: Bricks, Beads and Bones: The Harappan Civilisation

questions.text: हड़प्पाई लिपि के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कथन सही नहीं है?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following is not a true statement regarding Harappan Script?

options.A: यह लिपि आज तक पढ़ी नहीं जा सकी।
options.B: यह लिपि बाईं से दाईं ओर लिखी जाती थी।
options.D: इसमें चिह्नों की संख्या 375 से 400 के बीच थी।

options_english.A: This script remains undeciphered till date.
options_english.B: This script was written from left to right.
options_english.D: It has too many signs between 375 and 400.

questions.solution: Option B is the correct choice because the Harappan script was generally written from right to left, not left to right. Options A, C, and D are all accurate facts about the Harappan script; it remains undeciphered, it is not alphabetic (it contains many signs), and the sign count is indeed between 375 and 400.
questions.chapter: Bricks, Beads and Bones: The Harappan Civilisation

questions.text: निम्नलिखित चित्र की दिए गए विकल्पों में से पहचान कीजिए:
questions.text_english: Identify the following picture from the given options:
questions.image_description: A formal portrait of a woman wearing royal attire, including a crown and a long heavy robe.
questions.solution: The image provided is that of Sultan Jahan Begum, who was a prominent ruler of Bhopal and instrumental in the preservation of the Sanchi Stupa. Other options like Jahanara Begum were Mughal princesses, and Shahjahan Begum was another ruler of Bhopal, but the photograph specifically represents Sultan Jahan Begum.
questions.chapter: Thinkers, Beliefs and Buildings: Cultural Developments

questions.text: _______ प्रथा एक पुरुष की अनेक पत्नियाँ होने की सामाजिक परिपाटी है।
questions.text_english: The practice of _______ means a man having several wives.
questions.solution: The correct term for a man having several wives is Polygyny (बहुपत्नी). Polyandry refers to a woman having multiple husbands, while Exogamy and Endogamy refer to marriage outside or inside specific social groups respectively.
questions.chapter: Kinship, Caste and Class: Early Societies

questions.text: निम्नलिखित को कालक्रमिक क्रम से व्यवस्थित कीजिए:
questions.text_english: Arrange the following in chronological order:
questions.instruction_line: I. अशोक का शासन, II. सिकंदर का आक्रमण, III. गुप्त वंश का शासन, IV. कर्नाटक में चालुक्यों का उदय
questions.instruction_line_english: I. Rule of Ashoka, II. Invasion of Alexander, III. Rule of Gupta dynasty, IV. Rise of Chalukyas in Karnataka
questions.solution: The chronological order is: Alexander's invasion (c. 326 BCE), Ashoka's rule (c. 268-232 BCE), the Gupta dynasty (c. 320 CE onwards), and finally the rise of the Chalukyas (c. 6th century CE). Thus, option C (II, I, III, IV) is the correct sequence.
questions.chapter: Kings, Farmers and Towns: Early States and Economies

questions.text: अभिकथन (A): आठवीं सदी के कैलाशनाथ मंदिर को पहाड़ी काट कर बनाया गया था। कारण (R): मंदिरों को पहाड़ काट कर कृत्रिम गुफाओं का रूप देने का आदेश राजा अशोक ने दिया था।
questions.text_english: Assertion (A): In the Eighth Century, the Kailashnath Temple was carved out of mountain. Reason (R): King Ashoka had given the directive to create artificial caves by cutting into the mountains to resemble temples.

options.A: (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं और (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।

options_english.A: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options_english.B: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution: The Assertion is true as the Kailashnath Temple was carved from rock. The Reason is untrue because it was the Mauryan Emperor Ashoka who commissioned the earliest rock-cut caves, but those were for the Ajivikas, not specifically to resemble temples for later dynasties. Thus, (A) is true but (R) is false.
questions.chapter: Thinkers, Beliefs and Buildings: Cultural Developments

questions.text: निम्नलिखित जानकारी की सहायता से मध्यकालीन विश्व-यात्री की पहचान कीजिए: 1332-33 में भारत के लिए प्रस्थान करने से पहले वह मक्का की तीर्थ यात्रा कर चुका था। दिल्ली के सुल्तान, मुहम्मद बिन तुग़लक ने उसे दिल्ली का काज़ी या न्यायाधीश नियुक्त किया।
questions.text_english: Identify the medieval globe-trotter with the help of the following information: Before he set-off for India he made pilgrimage trips to Mecca before 1332-33 C.E. The Delhi Sultan Muhammad Bin Tughlaq made him Qazi or the judge of Delhi.
questions.solution: Ibn Batuta is the correct answer. He was a Moroccan traveler who visited India during the reign of Muhammad Bin Tughlaq, who famously appointed him as the Qazi (judge) of Delhi.
questions.chapter: Through the Eyes of Travellers: Perceptions of Society

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से सिक्खों के किस गुरु ने 'आदि ग्रंथ साहिब' का संकलन किया?
questions.text_english: Who among the following Sikh Gurus compiled 'Adi Granth Sahib'?
questions.solution: Guru Arjun Dev Ji, the fifth Sikh Guru, compiled the Adi Granth in 1604, which included the hymns of his predecessors and those of other saints like Baba Farid, Ravidas, and Kabir.
questions.chapter: Bhakti-Sufi Traditions: Changes in Religious Beliefs

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से वीरशैव परंपरा के संदर्भ में सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए:
questions.text_english: Choose the correct option regarding Virashaiva tradition from the following:

options.A: इस परंपरा का उद्भव कर्नाटक में हुआ।
options.C: वे पुनर्जन्म के सिद्धांत को मानते थे।
options.D: वे श्राद्ध संस्कार का पालन करते थे।

options_english.B: They are the followers of Vishnu.
options_english.C: They believed in the theory of rebirth.

questions.solution: The Virashaiva tradition (Lingayats) emerged in Karnataka during the 12th century under the leadership of Basavanna. They were followers of Shiva (not Vishnu) and rejected practices like rebirth theory and funerary rites, instead practicing burial.
questions.chapter: Bhakti-Sufi Traditions: Changes in Religious Beliefs

questions.text: निम्नलिखित जानकारी को ध्यानपूर्वक पढ़िए और इस दरगाह का स्थान नीचे दिए विकल्पों में से पहचानिए: यह शेख सलीम चिश्ती की दरगाह है। अकबर ने इस दरगाह का कई बार दौरा किया।
questions.text_english: Read the following information carefully and choose the correct location for this dargah from the given options: It is a dargah of Shaikh Salim Chisti. Akbar visited this dargah many a times.
questions.solution: The Dargah of Shaikh Salim Chishti is located in Fatehpur Sikri. Akbar held the saint in high regard, which led him to establish his capital at Fatehpur Sikri near the saint's residence.
questions.chapter: Bhakti-Sufi Traditions: Changes in Religious Beliefs

questions.text: मुगल ग्रामीण समाज का निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा विवरण सुमेलित है?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following description of Mughal rural society is correctly matched?
questions.image_description: A table showing groups and their professions.
questions.solution: In the Mughal administrative system, a 'Mansabdar' held a rank that entailed both military and bureaucratic duties. Other matches provided (Raiyat-Boatsman, Mallah-Banker, Shroff-Peasant) are incorrect; Raiyat means peasant, and Shroffs were money changers/bankers.
questions.chapter: Peasants, Zamindars and the State: Agrarian Society

questions.text: स्तंभ-I का मिलान स्तंभ-II से कीजिए और सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए:
questions.text_english: Match column-I with column-II and choose the correct option:
questions.instruction_line: Column-I: I. Brihadeswara, II. Channekeshwar, III. Hazara Ram, IV. Chidambaram. Column-II: A. Vijayanagar, B. Tanjavur, C. Tamil Nadu, D. Belur
questions.instruction_line_english: Column-I: I. Brihadeswara, II. Channekeshwar, III. Hazara Ram, IV. Chidambaram. Column-II: A. Vijayanagar, B. Tanjavur, C. Tamil Nadu, D. Belur
questions.image_description: A table matching temples to regions.
questions.solution: Brihadeswara is in Tanjavur (I-B), Channekeshwar is in Belur (II-D), Hazara Ram is in Vijayanagar (III-A), and Chidambaram is in Tamil Nadu (IV-C). Thus, the matching sequence I-B, II-D, III-A, IV-C corresponds to Option C.
questions.chapter: An Imperial Capital: Vijayanagara

questions.text: निम्नलिखित जानकारी की सहायता से सोलहवीं और सत्रहवीं शताब्दी के दौरान जंगली कबीले की पहचान कीजिए: असम में ये जंगली कबीलों के सरदार राजा बन गए। ये ज़मीन के बदले सैनिक सेवा देते थे। इन्होंने जंगली हाथी पकड़ने पर अपने एकाधिकार का ऐलान कर रखा था।
questions.text_english: Identify the forest tribe during sixteenth and seventeenth century with the help of following information: In Assam these Tribal Chiefs became kings. They rendered military service in exchange of land. They declared their monopoly on catching wild elephants.
questions.solution: The Ahom tribe rose to prominence in Assam, where their tribal chiefs transitioned into kings and exercised control over resources like wild elephants, which were essential for military purposes.
questions.chapter: Peasants, Zamindars and the State: Agrarian Society

questions.text: बंगाल में इस्तमरारी बंदोबस्त लागू करने में अंग्रेजों के प्राथमिक उद्देश्य की पहचान कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Identify the primary purpose of Britishers to implement Permanent Settlement in Bengal.

options.A: क्षेत्र के किसानों को सशक्त करने के लिए।
options.B: क्षेत्र में भू-स्वामित्व को समाप्त करने के लिए।
options.C: ज़ोतदारों का कृषि उत्पादन बढ़ाने के लिए।
options.D: ब्रिटिश सरकार को वित्तीय स्थिरता प्रदान करने के लिए।

options_english.A: To empower peasants of the region.
options_english.B: To abolish land ownership in the region.
options_english.C: To increase agricultural productivity of Jotedars.
options_english.D: To provide financial stability to British govt.

questions.solution: The primary purpose of the Permanent Settlement implemented by Lord Cornwallis was to ensure a fixed, regular revenue income for the British government, thereby providing financial stability.
questions.chapter: Colonialism and the Countryside: Exploring Official Archives

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन बिहार क्षेत्र से 1857 के विद्रोह का नेता था?
questions.text_english: Who among the following was the leader of the revolt of 1857 from Bihar region?
questions.solution: Kunwar Singh, the elderly zamindar of Jagdishpur, was the leader of the 1857 revolt in the Bihar region.
questions.chapter: Rebels and the Raj: 1857 Revolt

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से किसने अवध साम्राज्य के लिए नीचे दी गई पंक्ति का वर्णन किया? ये चैरी फल एक दिन हमारे ही मुँह में आकर गिरेगा।
questions.text_english: Who among the following described the following line for Kingdom of Awadh? A cherry that will fall into our mouth one day.
questions.solution: Lord Dalhousie described the kingdom of Awadh as a 'cherry that will drop into our mouths one day', indicating its inevitable annexation, which eventually happened in 1856.
questions.chapter: Rebels and the Raj: 1857 Revolt

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से किस स्थान पर 10 मई, 1857 को विद्रोह शुरू हुआ?
questions.text_english: At which of the following places the mutiny broke out on 10th day of May 1857?
questions.solution: The mutiny of 1857 officially broke out on May 10, 1857, at the Meerut Cantonment, from where the soldiers marched to Delhi.
questions.chapter: Rebels and the Raj: 1857 Revolt

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से किसने संविधान सभा में प्रस्ताव पेश किया कि भारतीय राष्ट्रीय ध्वज केसरिया, सफेद और गहरे हरे रंग का समान अनुपात में क्षैतिज तिरंगा होगा और केंद्र में नीले रंग का चक्र होगा?
questions.text_english: Who among the following moved the resolution in the Constituent Assembly that the Indian National Flag be horizontal tricolour of saffron, white and dark green in equal proportions with a wheel in navy blue in the centre?
questions.solution: Jawaharlal Nehru moved the resolution for the national flag in the Constituent Assembly, defining its colors and the Ashoka Chakra in the center.
questions.chapter: Frames of the Constitution: The Beginning of a New Era

questions.text: नीचे दी गई जानकारी की सहायता से संविधान सभा के सदस्य की पहचान कीजिए: (i) वह संविधान की प्रारूप समिति के सदस्य थे। (ii) वह एक वकील थे। (iii) इन्होंने संविधान का प्रारूप तैयार करने के लिए महत्वपूर्ण सुझाव दिए। (iv) वह मद्रास (चेन्नई) के रहने वाले थे।
questions.text_english: Identify the member of Constituent Assembly with the help of information given below: (i) He was a member of drafting committee of constitution. (ii) He was a lawyer. (iii) He gave crucial inputs in drafting of constitution. (iv) He belonged to Madras (Chennai).
questions.solution: Alladi Krishnaswami Ayyar was an eminent lawyer from Madras and a key member of the Constituent Assembly's Drafting Committee, providing crucial inputs during the drafting process.
questions.chapter: Frames of the Constitution: The Beginning of a New Era

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से किस आंदोलन को 'लाल-बाल-पाल' ने व्यापक बनाया और 1905-1907 तक अपने संघर्ष को 'अखिल भारतीय चरित्र' के रूप में व्यक्त किया?
questions.text_english: Which of the following movements was broadened by 'Lal-Bal-Pal' and conveyed it as the all-India character of their struggle from 1905-1907?
questions.solution: The Swadeshi Movement (1905-1907) was led by the extremist faction of the Congress, famously known as 'Lal-Bal-Pal' (Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, and Bipin Chandra Pal), who transformed it into a broad-based, all-India struggle.
questions.chapter: Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement

questions.text: (a) अपने शिल्प उत्पादन के लिए कच्चा माल प्राप्त करने के लिए हड़प्पावासियों द्वारा अपनाए गए तरीकों को स्पष्ट कीजिए। अथवा (b) पुरातत्वविद् हड़प्पावासियों की आहार संबंधी आदतों का पुनर्निर्माण करने में कैसे सक्षम हुए हैं? स्पष्ट कीजिए।
questions.text_english: (a) Explain the strategies adopted by Harappans to procure raw material for their craft production. OR (b) Explain how archaeologists have been able to reconstruct dietary practices of the Harappans.

key_points: Procurement of raw materials like copper, stones, wood, etc. from local and distant areas.
Establishment of settlements near sources of raw materials like Shortughai for lapis lazuli.
Sending expeditions to regions like Khetri (Rajasthan) for copper or South India for gold.

questions.solution: The Harappans employed diverse strategies to acquire raw materials. Firstly, they established settlements near resource-rich zones, such as Shortughai in Afghanistan, which was close to the source of the highly valued blue stone, lapis lazuli. Secondly, they sent specialized expeditions to areas like Khetri in Rajasthan for copper and to South India for gold. Furthermore, they engaged in long-distance trade, establishing contacts with regions like Oman and Mesopotamia to procure materials that were not available locally, ensuring a steady supply for their complex craft production system.
questions.chapter: Bricks, Beads and Bones: The Harappan Civilisation

questions.text: छठी शताब्दी ईसा पूर्व के बाद से कुलीन परिवारों के बीच पितृवंशीय व्यवस्था कैसे महत्त्वपूर्ण थी? उदाहरणों सहित स्पष्ट कीजिए।
questions.text_english: How was patriliny system important among the elite families from sixth century BCE onwards. Explain with examples.

key_points: Patriliny means tracing descent from father to son.
It helped in maintaining family lineage and property control.
Example: Mahabharata, where the conflict was over the patrilineal throne.

questions.solution: Patriliny refers to the system where descent is traced from father to son, grandson, and so on. In elite families from the sixth century BCE, this system was crucial for consolidating power and property. Since kingship was generally patrilineal, it ensured that the throne remained within the male line of the family. The epic Mahabharata provides a vivid example of this, as the core of the conflict between the Kauravas and the Pandavas revolved around the control of the patrilineal Kuru throne, emphasizing the significance of this structure in elite social dynamics.
questions.chapter: Kinship, Caste and Class: Early Societies

questions.text: बाबा गुरु नानक देव जी ने निर्गुण भक्ति का प्रचार किया। इस कथन की व्याख्या कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Baba Guru Nanak Dev ji advocated a form of Nirguna Bhakti. Substantiate the statement.

key_points: Nirguna Bhakti emphasizes devotion to a formless God.
Guru Nanak rejected rituals, idol worship, and caste distinctions.
He preached absolute oneness of God and salvation through remembrance.

questions.solution: Baba Guru Nanak Dev Ji advocated Nirguna Bhakti, which centers on devotion to a formless, abstract divinity. He strongly rejected external rituals, idol worship, and the rigid caste-based distinctions prevalent in society. Instead, he taught that God is absolute, formless, and omnipresent. For Guru Nanak, true religious practice involved sincere meditation, the remembrance of God’s name, and leading a life of honest, humble labor. He aimed to build a community where spiritual salvation was accessible to all individuals regardless of their social background or gender.
questions.chapter: Bhakti-Sufi Traditions: Changes in Religious Beliefs

questions.text: आइन-ए-अकबरी को सोलहवीं और सत्रहवीं शताब्दी के कृषि इतिहास का एक महत्त्वपूर्ण स्रोत माना जाता है।इस कथन की परख कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Ain-i-Akbari is considered a major source for the agrarian history of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries. Examine the statement.

key_points: Provides detailed statistical data about Mughal administration and land.
Contains records on crops, revenue systems, and agrarian production.
Offers insight into the social and economic conditions of peasants.

questions.solution: The Ain-i-Akbari, written by Abu'l Fazl, is an indispensable record for understanding the agrarian history of the Mughal period. It provides exhaustive statistical data concerning the Mughal empire, including detailed information about crops grown, regional variations in agricultural production, and the complex revenue assessment systems. By documenting the fiscal and administrative structure of land use, it offers scholars profound insights into the economic life of peasants and the role of the state in agrarian production during the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.
questions.chapter: Peasants, Zamindars and the State: Agrarian Society

questions.text: (a) बहादुरशाह ज़फर ने 1857 के विद्रोहियों को किन परिस्थितियों में अपना आशीर्वाद दिया? स्पष्ट कीजिए। अथवा (b) 1857 के विद्रोह को जानने के किन्हीं तीन स्रोतों को स्पष्ट कीजिए।
questions.text_english: (a) Under what circumstances did Bahadur Shah Zafar bless the rebellion of 1857? Explain. OR (b) Explain any three sources to know about the Revolt of 1857.

key_points: Rebels from Meerut arrived in Delhi and demanded support.
Bahadur Shah Zafar was reluctant initially due to age and lack of power.
He ultimately relented and became the symbolic leader of the revolt.

questions.solution: When the rebellious sepoys from Meerut arrived in Delhi, they stormed the Red Fort and demanded that Bahadur Shah Zafar, the Mughal Emperor, lead their uprising. Initially, Zafar was hesitant; he was aged, lacked real political power, and was wary of the British. However, faced with the overwhelming insistence and persistence of the mutinous soldiers, he ultimately accepted the leadership, becoming the symbolic figurehead of the revolt against British rule.
questions.chapter: Rebels and the Raj: 1857 Revolt

questions.text: “संविधान के मसविदे में संघवाद के मुद्दे पर विषयों की तीन सूचियाँ बनाई गईं।” इस कथन को उदाहरणों सहित स्पष्ट कीजिए।
questions.text_english: The draft constitution provided for three lists of subjects on the issue of federalism. Explain the statement with examples.

key_points: Union List: Subjects under central control (e.g., Defence, Foreign Affairs).
State List: Subjects for state governments (e.g., Police, Agriculture).
Concurrent List: Subjects shared by both (e.g., Education, Forests).

questions.solution: To manage federalism, the Indian Constitution established three lists. The Union List covers subjects of national importance managed by the central government, such as Defence, Railways, and Foreign Affairs. The State List includes subjects handled by state governments, such as Police, Trade, and Agriculture. The Concurrent List contains subjects where both the center and states have jurisdiction, such as Education, Forest, and Marriage laws. This distribution prevents conflicts and ensures balanced administration between the center and the states.
questions.chapter: Frames of the Constitution: The Beginning of a New Era

questions.text: (a) आरंभिक भारतीय इतिहास में छठी शताब्दी ईसा पूर्व आरंभिक राज्यों, साम्राज्यों और विभिन्न विचारधाराओं के उद्भव का काल था। इस कथन को न्यायसंगत ठहराइये। अथवा (b) हालाँकि अभिलेख इतिहास के पुनर्निमाण के लिए मजबूत साक्ष्य प्रदान करते हैं फिर भी इन साक्ष्यों की कुछ सीमाएँ हैं।इस कथन को न्यायसंगत ठहराइये।
questions.text_english: (a) The sixth century BCE was a period of emergence of early states, empires and diverse thoughts in the early Indian history.Justify the statement. OR (b) Although inscriptions provide strong evidence for reconstructing history yet there are few limitations to these evidences. Justify the statement.

key_points: Introduction to 6th Century BCE as a 'turning point'.
Rise of sixteen Mahajanapadas and urbanization.
Emergence of Buddhism, Jainism, and new philosophical thoughts.
Development of coinage and organized administration.
Conclusion on the significance of this era.

questions.solution: The sixth century BCE is often regarded as a major turning point in early Indian history. It witnessed the emergence of the sixteen Mahajanapadas, characterized by the rise of early states and complex political structures like Magadha. This era saw the growth of urbanization, the introduction of systematic taxation, and the use of iron, which transformed agriculture and warfare. Simultaneously, it was a period of great intellectual churning, witnessing the birth of Buddhism and Jainism, which challenged traditional Vedic orthodoxy. These diverse thoughts and the evolution of political empires laid the foundation for subsequent Indian history, marking the transition into a new socio-economic order.
questions.chapter: Kings, Farmers and Towns: Early States and Economies

questions.text: (a) विजयनगर साम्राज्य के उत्थान और पतन के मुख्य कारणों की परख कीजिए। अथवा (b) विजयनगर साम्राज्य की किलेबंदी के विशिष्ट पहलुओं की परख कीजिए।
questions.text_english: (a) Examine the main reasons for the rise and decline of the Vijaynagar empire. OR (b) Examine the distinctive aspects of the fortification of the Vijaynagar empire.

key_points: Rise: Founded by Harihara and Bukka, military strategy, trade prosperity.
Decline: Internal instability, defeats against Deccan Sultanates.
Fortification: Multi-layered walls, water management, agricultural integration.

questions.solution: The Vijayanagara Empire, founded by Harihara and Bukka in 1336, rose to power due to a strong military and flourishing trade networks, acting as a bulwark against Northern incursions. Its growth was supported by highly efficient administrative and agricultural policies. However, its decline in the late 16th century was due to multiple factors, including constant warfare with the Deccan Sultanates, dynastic succession struggles, and the devastating defeat at the Battle of Talikota in 1565. This defeat led to the eventual destruction and abandonment of the capital city, marking the end of a golden era for the southern Indian empire.
questions.chapter: An Imperial Capital: Vijayanagara

questions.text: (a) गाँधीजी के 'नमक सत्याग्रह' शुरू करने के निर्णय के पीछे के कारणों को स्पष्ट कीजिए और यह आंदोलन एक महत्त्वपूर्ण घटना क्यों बन गया? अथवा (b) 'भारत छोड़ो आंदोलन' को जन आंदोलन क्यों माना गया? स्पष्ट कीजिए।
questions.text_english: (a) Explain the reasons behind Gandhiji's decision to initiate the Salt Satyagraha and why did this movement become a significant event? OR (b) Explain why the 'Quit India Movement' was considered a mass movement.

key_points: Salt tax as a moral issue affecting all sections of society.
Dandi March as a symbol of defiance against British rule.
Significance: International attention, mass participation of women and youth.

questions.solution: Gandhiji decided to initiate the Salt Satyagraha because the salt tax was a highly symbolic issue that united all sections of Indian society, including the poor and rich. By choosing salt, a basic necessity, Gandhiji turned a moral issue into a political one. The Dandi March became a significant event because it effectively mobilized the masses, drew unprecedented international attention, and saw widespread, peaceful defiance of British laws. It marked a turning point in the struggle, as it encouraged women's participation and demonstrated the power of non-violent resistance on a national scale.
questions.chapter: Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement

questions.text:
व्यवहार में बौद्ध धर्म

सुत्त पिटक से लिए गए इस उद्धरण में बुद्ध सिगल नाम के एक अमीर गृहपति को सलाह दे रहे हैं:

मालिक को अपने नौकरों और कर्मचारियों की पाँच तरह से देखभाल करनी चाहिए.... उनकी क्षमता के अनुसार उन्हें काम देकर, उन्हें भोजन और मज़दूरी देकर, बीमार पड़ने पर उनकी परिचर्या करके, उनके साथ सुस्वादु भोजन बाँटकर और समय-समय पर उन्हें छुट्टी देकर...

कुल के लोगों को पाँच तरह से श्रमणों (जिन्होंने सांसारिक जीवन को त्याग दिया है) और ब्राह्मणों की देखभाल करनी चाहिए.... कर्म, वचन और मन से अनुराग द्वारा, उनके स्वागत में हमेशा घर खुले रखकर और उनकी दिन-प्रतिदिन की ज़रूरतों की पूर्ति करके।

सिगल को माता-पिता, शिक्षक और पत्नी के साथ व्यवहार के लिए भी ऐसे ही उपदेश दिए गए हैं।
questions.text_english:
Buddhism in practice

This is an excerpt from the Sutta Pitaka, and contains the advice given by the Buddha to a wealthy householder named Sigala:

In five ways should a master look after his servants and employees.... by assigning them work according to their strength, by supplying them with food and wages, by tending them in sickness;

by sharing delicacies with them and by granting leave at times...

In five ways should the clansmen look after the needs of samanas (those who have renounced the world) and Brahmanas: by affection in act and speech and mind, by keeping open house to them and supplying their worldly needs.

There are similar instructions to Sigala about how to behave with his parents, teacher and wife.

sub_questions.text: बौद्ध धर्म में सुत्त पिटक के महत्त्व को स्पष्ट कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the significance of Sutta Pitaka in Buddhism.
sub_questions.solution: The Sutta Pitaka is significant because it contains the main teachings, dialogues, and sermons of the Buddha, providing the foundational ethical and religious guidelines for Buddhist followers.

sub_questions.text: बुद्ध ने अमीर गृहपति को मानवीय और नैतिक बनने की सलाह कैसे दी?
sub_questions.text_english: How did Buddha advise the wealthy householders to be humane and ethical?
sub_questions.solution: Buddha advised householders to be ethical by treating employees with fairness (fair wages, care in sickness), showing respect to renunciants (Samanas/Brahmanas), and fulfilling social responsibilities toward family and teachers.

sub_questions.text: बुद्ध ने सिगल को अपने माता-पिता और शिक्षकों के साथ कैसा व्यवहार करना चाहिए, इस बारे में क्या सलाह दी?
sub_questions.text_english: What was the advice given by Buddha to Sigala on how to behave with his parents and teachers?
sub_questions.solution: Buddha advised that householders should treat parents and teachers with respect and affection. He emphasized that proper behavior, both in speech and deed, is essential for maintaining harmonious relationships with those who guide and nurture one throughout life.

questions.chapter: Thinkers, Beliefs and Buildings: Cultural Developments

questions.text:
विशाल पहुँच वाली एक भाषा

संस्कृत के विषय में अल-बिरूनी यह लिखता है:

यदि आप इस कठिनाई (संस्कृत भाषा सीखने की) से पार पाना चाहते हैं तो यह आसान नहीं होगा क्योंकि अरबी भाषा की तरह ही, शब्दों तथा विभक्तियों, दोनों में ही इस भाषा की पहुँच बहुत विस्तृत है। इसमें एक ही वस्तु के लिए कई शब्द, मूल तथा व्युत्पन्न दोनों, प्रयुक्त होते हैं और एक ही शब्द का प्रयोग कई वस्तुओं के लिए होता है, जिन्हें भली प्रकार समझने के लिए विभिन्न विशेषक संकेतपदों के माध्यम से एक दूसरे से अलग किया जाना आवश्यक है।
questions.text_english:
A language with an enormous range

Al-Biruni described Sanskrit as follows:

If you want to conquer this difficulty (i.e. to learn Sanskrit), you will not find it easy, because the language is of an enormous range, both in words and inflections, something like the Arabic, calling one and the same thing by various names, both original and derivative, and using one and the same word for a variety of subjects, which, in order to be properly understood, must be distinguished from each other by various qualifying epithets.

sub_questions.text: अल-बिरूनी को संस्कृत का अध्ययन करने के लिए किस चीज़ ने प्रेरित किया?
sub_questions.text_english: What motivated Al-Biruni to study Sanskrit?
sub_questions.solution: Al-Biruni was motivated to study Sanskrit to understand Indian intellectual and religious texts, which he found complex but essential for cross-cultural knowledge.

sub_questions.text: संस्कृत के बारे में अल-बिरूनी की टिप्पणियों ने अंतर-संस्कृतिक समझ में कैसे योगदान दिया?
sub_questions.text_english: How did Al-Biruni's observations about Sanskrit contribute to cross cultural understanding?
sub_questions.solution: By comparing Sanskrit to Arabic, he helped Islamic scholars recognize the complexity and richness of Indian literature, bridging the intellectual gap between the two cultures.

sub_questions.text: अल-बिरूनी ने संस्कृत की तुलना अरबी से किस प्रकार की?
sub_questions.text_english: In what ways Al-Biruni compare Sanskrit to Arabic?
sub_questions.solution: Al-Biruni noted that both Sanskrit and Arabic have an enormous range in words and inflections. He observed that both languages use a variety of names for a single object (derivative or original) and employ single words for multiple meanings, necessitating careful use of qualifying epithets for clarity.

questions.chapter: Through the Eyes of Travellers: Perceptions of Society

questions.text:
रैयत अर्जी

नीचे एक याचिका का उदाहरण दिया गया है जो करजत तालुका के मीरगाँव के एक रैयत द्वारा कलेक्टर, अहमदनगर, दक्कन दंगा आयोग को दी गई थी:

साहूकार लोग काफी दिनों से हम पर अत्याचार कर रहे हैं। चूँकि हम अपना घर खर्च चलाने के लिए काफी मात्रा में पैसा नहीं कमा सकते, इसलिए हम उनसे पैसा, कपड़ा और अनाज़ माँगने के लिए मजबूर हो गए हैं। उनसे हमें ये चीजें मिलती जाती हैं पर बड़ी कठिनाई से और उसके लिए हमें उनके साथ कड़ी शर्तों पर बंधपत्र लिखने के लिए मजबूर होना पड़ता है। इसके अलावा कपड़ा और अनाज भी नकद दरों पर नहीं बेचा जाता। हमसे जो कीमतें माँगी जाती हैं वह नकदी कीमत चुकाने वाले ग्राहकों की अपेक्षा आमतौर पर 25 से 50 प्रतिशत ज्यादा होती हैं। हमारे खेतों की उपज भी साहूकार ले जाते हैं; उपज ले जाते समय तो वे हमें यह आश्वासन देते हैं कि इसकी कीमत हमारे खाते में जमा कर दी जाएगी लेकिन वे हमारे खातों में ऐसा कोई उल्लेख नहीं करते। वे जब हमारी उपज ले जाते हैं तो बदले में कोई रसीद भी नहीं देते।
questions.text_english:
A ryot petition

This is an example of a petition from a ryot of the village of Mirajgaon, Taluka Karjat, to the Collector, Ahmednagar, Deccan Riots Commission:

The sowkars (sahukars).... have of late begun to oppress us. As we cannot earn enough to defray our household expenses, we are actually forced to beg of them to provide us with money, clothes and grain, which we obtain from them not without great difficulty, nor without their compelling us to enter into hard conditions in the bond.

Moreover the necessary clothes and grain are not sold to us at cash rates. The prices asked from us are generally twenty-five or fifty per cent more than demanded from customers making ready money payments... The produce of our fields is also taken by the sowkars, who at the time of removing it assure us that it will be credited to our account, but they do not actually make any mention of it in the accounts. They also refuse to pass us any receipts for the produce so removed by them.

sub_questions.text: साहूकार रैयतों पर किस प्रकार से अत्याचार करते थे?
sub_questions.text_english: In what ways the money-lenders oppressed the ryots?
sub_questions.solution: Money-lenders oppressed ryots by forcing them into hard bond conditions, charging 25-50% higher prices for essential goods, and refusing to issue receipts for the agricultural produce they seized.

sub_questions.text: साहूकारों द्वारा अनाज क्यों छीना गया?
sub_questions.text_english: Why was the harvest taken away by the money-lenders?
sub_questions.solution: The money-lenders took the harvest as a way to recover debts, often without officially crediting the ryots' accounts or providing any formal receipt, thereby continuing the cycle of exploitation.

sub_questions.text: रैयतवारी व्यवस्था की किन्हीं दो विशेषताओं की व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain any two features of the Ryotwari system.
sub_questions.solution: Two features of the Ryotwari system were: First, the land revenue was collected directly from the cultivators (ryots) by the state without any middlemen like zamindars. Second, the revenue assessments were often high and periodically revised, which burdened the peasants significantly.

questions.chapter: Colonialism and the Countryside: Exploring Official Archives

questions.text: 34.1 दिए गए भारत के राजनीतिक रेखा-मानचित्र पर निम्नलिखित को उपयुक्त चिह्नों से अंकित कीजिए और उनके नाम लिखिए: (i) बनावली (विकसित हड़प्पा पुरास्थल), (ii) भरहुत (बौद्ध स्थल), (iii) (a) आगरा या (b) दिल्ली (मुगलों के अधीन क्षेत्र)। 34.2 दिए गए इसी राजनीतिक रेखा-मानचित्र पर दो स्थानों को A और B से अंकित किया गया है जो भारतीय राष्ट्रीय आंदोलन के केन्द्र थे। पहचानिए।
questions.text_english: 34.1 On the given political outline map of India, locate and label the following with appropriate signs: (i) Banawali (A matured Harappan Site), (ii) Bharhut (A Buddhist Site), (iii) (a) Agra or (b) Delhi (Territory under Mughal's control). 34.2 On the same map two places have been marked as A and B, which are the centres of Indian National Movement. Identify them.

key_points: Banawali: Haryana
Bharhut: Madhya Pradesh
Agra/Delhi: UP/Delhi region
A (on map): Lahore/North India centre
B (on map): Bombay/West India centre

questions.solution: Banawali is located in the Haryana region. Bharhut is in the Satna district of Madhya Pradesh. Agra and Delhi are marked in the North-Indian plains region under Mughal control. Regarding the map markings, point A refers to Lahore and point B refers to Bombay, both being significant centers of the Indian National Movement.
